propositions: The generic reads-under-write-burst property does not detect partial-success cases (shape-valid, content-incomplete payloads like empty JSON or missing ticket_id) that the original CLI show test catches.

Fault-seeded evidence proves the original test and generic property are complementary rather than redundant: the original detects F3/F6 payload completeness; the generic detects F5/F7 stall/empty-output classes.
Consolidating the two tests by deleting the original would forfeit detection of two independent fault classes (F3 and F6) that the generic property's shape-only assertion does not cover.
The original test's protection value derives entirely from payload content validation, not from the six-round four-ticket storm; content incompleteness surfaces deterministically on round 0.
No consolidation savings are available: deleting the original test would cost detection capability; runtime optimization must come from reducing storm size while retaining both oracles.
